name: ultra.research
description: ULTRA Research/Scraping studio: does the source say it, is it primary, does it contradict something settled? Counters, liveness and staleness arithmetic stay in code; only judgment is asked here.

claim_supported.instructions: The cited source itself states this specific claim; it is not the agent's inference or a different figure.

source_grade.instructions: How strong is this source as evidence

criteria.HIGH: primary source, named method or first-hand measurement
criteria.MED: secondary but credible: reputable outlet restating a primary claim
criteria.LOW: blog, forum, undated, anonymous or self-interested with no method

is_primary.instructions: This is a primary source: the party that did or measured the thing is speaking.

contradicts_settled.instructions: This finding contradicts something the mission already settled, so the settled node needs reopening.

novelty.instructions: How does this competitor or analogue relate to what we are planning

criteria.same: does the same thing, for the same person, the same way
criteria.better: same mechanism, measurably better on one axis
criteria.different: different mechanism for the same job
criteria.new: no one here is attempting this

stale_risk.instructions: How likely is this source to have drifted out of date since it was fetched
criteria: content is date-immobile or already re-verified this week
slow-moving; last fetch is recent enough to trust
moves on a monthly scale; last fetch is borderline
moves weekly or faster; a stale read would mislead the decision
moves daily or is known to have changed since the fetch
already contradicted by a fresher source on hand

rules.reason: citation does not carry the claim attached to it (source laundering)
weak source behind a load-bearing finding
source most likely secondary: back it with a primary before it settles a node
no primary source in this evidence chain
contradiction with a settled node must reopen it with evidence attached
this competitor already does exactly this: the novelty claim needs rework
staleness risk too high to cite as current

notes.claim_supported: doc signal r.claim_supported. Motivation: 3-13% of deep-research citations are fabricated URLs and the dominant failure in strong-model systems is orchestrator citation error (arxiv.org/abs/2604.03173, arxiv.org/html/2608.24306v1).
notes.stale_risk: doc signal r.stale_risk; levels are ordered by how fast the content moves, combined in code with fetched_at.
notes.novelty: doc signal r.novelty; feeds the tree's per-component novelty tag.
